    THE BEK GUIDE

    A little guidance.

    Everything you need to create voices on your own device.

    Available inside the app.
    No account or API key needed.

    START HERE

    From words to voice.

    Bek turns your text into speech and lets you clone a voice you have permission to use. Choose browser AI for generation on your browser GPU, or the optional Python service for generation through a local process.

    1. Set up an engine. Open Settings and choose where to run speech. Browser mode needs a one-time model download of about 1.9 GB. Wait for the model to be ready.
    2. Write your script. Paste text, import a .txt file, or use a sample. The script limit is 5,000 characters.
    3. Choose your voice. In Voice settings, use an AI voice or choose Clone my voice. Select the script language; Khmer is at the top of the list.
    4. Choose Full voice or Split voice. Full voice generates the whole script in one request. Split voice makes smaller clips you can hear as they finish.
    5. Generate and listen. Play the result, download WAV, or merge completed parts into one file.
    First visit? Use a current Chrome or Edge desktop browser. Open the app on localhost or an HTTPS address so WebGPU and microphone access can work.

    Make it comfortable

    The sun/moon button switches light and dark themes. Settings → Appearance also lets you follow your system theme. Your preference is saved on this device.

    Compare the engines →
    YOUR DEVICE

    Choose an engine.

    Both options run without a hosted voice API or API key. They use different model files and need separate setup.

    Browser and Python engines
    EngineDownloadRuns on
    Browser · WebGPUAbout 1.94 GBYour browser GPU, with shader-f16 support
    Local Python serviceAbout 5 GB of model weights, plus dependenciesApple Silicon MPS, NVIDIA CUDA, or CPU

    Browser model setup

    1. In Settings, choose This browser under Run speech on.
    2. Click Set up · 1.9 GB and wait for download and GPU preparation.
    3. After reloading, click Load saved model to load cached weights into GPU memory.

    Allow at least 2.2 GB of free browser site storage for model setup. GPU memory and compatibility vary by device. Completed download segments can be reused after cancelling and resuming setup.

    Storage belongs to the address. localhost and 127.0.0.1 have separate browser storage. Changing the hostname or port can make your cached model and saved voices appear missing. Return to the original address.

    For Python installation, follow Python setup. Docker and VPS deployments serve the browser app; they do not include Python inference.

    MAKE IT YOURS

    Clone or record a voice.

    In Voice settings → Choose your voice, select Clone my voice. Use a saved voice, upload a WAV sample, or record one in the browser.

    Record a sample

    1. Choose Record voice. If a sample is already selected, click Choose another sample first.
    2. Select the Khmer or English reading passage.
    3. Click Start recording and allow microphone access. Read naturally in a quiet room; aim for 10–20 seconds.
    4. Click Stop, listen to your recording, then click Use recording.
    5. Confirm that this is your voice or you have permission to clone it. Enter your script and generate.

    The minimum recording length is 3 seconds. Recording stops automatically at 30 seconds. Silent and too-short takes are rejected. You can cancel, discard, or record again.

    Upload an existing sample

    Choose Upload audio and select or drop a WAV file. References must be 3–30 seconds long and below 15 MB. A clear recording of one speaker works best.

    Save a voice for later

    After selecting a sample and confirming permission, expand Save this voice for later, give it a name, and save it. It will appear under My voices and in the saved-voice picker. Selecting a reference resets the permission checkbox.

    Microphone access starts only when you click Start recording. Use HTTPS for a remote deployment, or localhost for local use. If permission is denied, update the site’s microphone permission or upload a WAV.

    Only clone voices you own or have permission to use, and label shared output as AI-generated.

    GENERATE YOUR WAY

    Full voice or split voice?

    Full voiceSplit voice
    One request for the entire script. Audio appears when the request finishes.Short parts, around 200 characters each. Listen and download as parts finish.
    A simple choice for short scripts.A useful choice for long scripts and checking progress.

    Split mode prefers paragraph, sentence, and word boundaries and keeps Khmer character clusters together. The output choice is saved on this device and stays fixed during a run.

    Read the progress

    The overall bar counts completed parts. Each part’s bar is empty while waiting, animated during generation, and full when ready. Elapsed time shows how long the current part has been running. The engine does not provide an exact within-part percentage.

    Stop, continue, and merge

    • Stop after this part waits for the current request to finish, then stops the queue.
    • Continue remaining parts skips completed audio and uses the original voice and settings. Keep the original page open to continue.
    • Merge all parts joins completed WAV samples in script order without generating again. A stopped run can merge only the completed parts.

    Finished audio is saved as parts complete. Reloading preserves finished parts, but the in-memory voice/settings snapshot needed to continue unfinished generation is lost.

    Adjust delivery

    Choose the language your script is written in. The language menu adds a speaking direction; it does not translate the text. Add an optional direction such as “calm and a little slower.” Quality offers Fast, Balanced, and High; higher quality takes longer.

    Advanced settings contain voice guidance and an optional random seed. A seed can reduce variation between takes, but does not guarantee identical audio across hardware. AI voice characters are descriptions, not fixed speaker identities.

    KEEP YOUR WORK

    Downloads and saved audio.

    WAV audio

    Use Download WAV for the full result or merged output. Each completed split part has its own player and Download part link. Merging follows script order and keeps the original audio samples.

    Estimated subtitles

    Download SRT creates sentence-based subtitle timing estimated from text length and total audio duration. It is not word alignment. Review and adjust timing before publishing captions.

    My voices and Audio library

    My voices stores reference samples. Audio library stores generated runs, including completed parts. Open a multipart run to listen, download individual parts, or merge them later. Older single clips remain playable.

    Where data lives

    • Drafts, theme choices, voices, and generated audio belong to this browser and site address.
    • Browser engine model files are cached in site storage. Python weights live in the project’s .models directory.
    • Browser generation processes scripts and references in the browser. Python mode sends them to the loopback service on your computer.
    • Model setup downloads files from Hugging Face. Fonts and runtime assets are bundled with the application.
    Keep important audio as downloads. Clearing site data, browser eviction, private browsing, or switching address can remove or hide saved work. If storage is full, download completed audio before leaving the page.
    LOCAL SERVICE

    Set up the Python engine.

    Use Python 3.10–3.12. Start from a cloned copy of the repository. The first run installs dependencies and model setup downloads about 5 GB of weights.

    macOS or Linux

    git clone https://github.com/virakbuthchhan/bek-voice.git
cd bek-voice
./start-python.sh

    Windows PowerShell

    Install Python 3.12, clone the repository, and run these commands from its folder:

    py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\pip install -r local/requirements.txt
.venv\Scripts\python local/server.py

    Load the model

    1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765.
    2. Go to Settings → Run speech on → Local Python service.
    3. Click Load Python model and wait until the engine is ready.

    The service selects MPS, CUDA, or CPU automatically. On macOS/Linux, if acceleration fails, stop the service and start it on CPU:

    SORI_DEVICE=cpu ./start-python.sh
    One service per port. Stop local Docker Compose before running Python on its default port. The included Python service listens on loopback port 8765 and is intended for local use.

    Cached weights stay in .models. Restarting the service reloads the model but does not require downloading cached weights again.

    CLONE AND RUN

    Run with Docker Compose.

    Install Docker Desktop on Windows/macOS, or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin on Linux. No API key is needed.

    git clone https://github.com/virakbuthchhan/bek-voice.git
cd bek-voice
docker compose up -d --build

    Open http://localhost:8765 in a compatible desktop browser, set up the browser model, then generate speech.

    Inference runs in the visitor’s browser. The container serves static app files. It does not run the Python engine or use the Docker host’s GPU. Each browser downloads and caches its own model.

    Manage the app

    docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f
docker compose down

    Apply an update

    git pull
docker compose up -d --build

    Change the local port

    Copy .env.example to .env, set PORT=8876, and run the Compose command again. Open http://localhost:8876. The local Compose port is bound to loopback.

    Use the modern docker compose command. For a public deployment, follow Deploy on a VPS.

    DEPLOYMENT

    Deploy on a VPS with HTTPS.

    The VPS serves Bek while voice processing stays in each visitor’s browser. The included production stack uses Caddy for HTTPS.

    1. Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin on the VPS.
    2. Point your domain’s DNS A record to the VPS. Add an AAAA record only if IPv6 is routed to the server.
    3. Allow inbound TCP 80 and 443 and keep SSH access available. UDP 443 is optional for HTTP/3.
    4. Clone the repository and configure your domain.
    git clone https://github.com/virakbuthchhan/bek-voice.git
cd bek-voice
cp .env.example .env

    Edit .env with your actual hostname and certificate contact:

    DOMAIN=voice.your-domain.com
ACME_EMAIL=you@your-domain.com

    Start the standalone VPS stack:

    docker compose -f compose.vps.yaml up -d --build
docker compose -f compose.vps.yaml logs -f caddy

    Visit your HTTPS domain after DNS resolves and Caddy obtains a certificate. Use the same -f compose.vps.yaml argument for future updates, logs, and stopping the stack.

    Use the VPS file on its own. Do not combine it with compose.yaml. Remote WebGPU and microphone access need HTTPS; a plain HTTP VPS IP or LAN address is not a substitute.

    Caddy certificate data stays in named Docker volumes. Normal down preserves it; down -v removes it. If you already use a reverse proxy on 80/443, use the local Compose stack and forward HTTPS traffic to its loopback port instead.

    GET UNSTUCK

    Troubleshooting.

    WebGPU is unavailable

    Use current Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer, with hardware acceleration enabled. Open localhost or an HTTPS domain. The GPU must expose shader-f16. If the device is incompatible, try the Python engine.

    Model setup failed or storage is full

    Allow at least 2.2 GB of free browser site storage and access to Hugging Face. Resume setup to reuse completed download segments. Clearing site data removes cached models and saved voices/audio, so download important work before a full reset.

    Generation feels slow or stuck

    Check the current part’s elapsed time. Its animated bar indicates an active request, not an exact completion estimate. Long Full voice requests take longer before producing audio. Use Split voice and Fast quality for shorter previews. CPU generation can be slow.

    The Python engine is offline or the port is busy

    Run start-python.sh from the project folder and open http://127.0.0.1:8765. Stop Docker Compose if it is using that port. Load the Python model in Settings. Read the Python terminal for model or device errors.

    Unexpected keyword argument “seed”

    Update the repository with git pull and restart the Python service. The fixed backend seeds its random generators without passing the unsupported keyword to VoxCPM 2.0.3. Cached model weights do not need to be downloaded again.

    Microphone permission was denied

    Allow microphone access for this site in the browser’s settings, then try Start recording again. Use HTTPS on a remote host. Upload a 3–30 second WAV sample if recording is unavailable.

    My saved voices or model disappeared

    Return to the same browser, profile, hostname, and port. localhost and 127.0.0.1 store data separately. Clearing site data, private browsing, or cache eviction can remove saved work. Use downloaded audio as your backup.

    The new interface does not appear

    Refresh or close and reopen the page. For Docker, pull the latest code and rebuild the container. Avoid clearing site data unless you intend to reset the cached model and saved work.

    The VPS HTTPS certificate is not issued

    Check DNS, including AAAA records, access to ports 80/443, and the Caddy logs. Make sure no other service is occupying those ports and certificate volumes remain writable.
